account: Today I inspected the mill and found 128 hay bales in the sale chest. No shortage or delivery order was confirmed, and I left the stock untouched. Freight offered available warehouse storage and said they would ask the baker about definite transport needs before moving grain. The neighbour has been exchanging this news with us. There has also been an unspecified rumour about a bridge or port change. I have no evidence that such a change exists: the secretary reports that the builder found no confirmed hazard, work or costs, and that the baker denied announcing a crossing or delivery change and confirmed normal operations. The innkeeper reportedly had only an unspecified rumour. This seems to be ordinary inquiries and news passing between townspeople, but I do not know where the rumour began or whether there is any purpose behind it. No grain transport or repair spending has been authorized by me. No council letters had reached the secretary by my thirteen o'clock appointment; I asked for the hall tables to be checked and for updates when I returned. After a quiet tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage, I have now returned to town hall at 16:33 for my half-past-four office appointment. The secretary is waiting inside; I have not yet heard whether anything new has arrived.
